doc.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022

chapter: Cecil Taylor and the new music
title: Cecil Taylor's personality and borrowed records
summary: Taylor's curiosity and strong opinions; he borrowed contemporary-composer records and returned them scratched.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Did you feel that his personality was reflected in his music that seemed to always be seeking the far boundaries? I may not be speaking exactly on point here but did he have a personality that reflected the way he played?

He had a conversation that reflected the way he played. His personality was that of one that you would recognize, a very, very, very smart person who had a mind that was flying all over the place as he talked, who was extremely curious about all manner of things and had strong opinions about all manner of things. He used to borrow my records of contemporary composers, Cage and Morton Feldman and others, Stockhausen — he would borrow those until I stopped lending them to him because he’d always give them back all scratched up. And he got very angry about that, I don’t think he ever forgave me for that. So he was always, always exploring and always curious. But he was also very, very serious and made certain that he studied the roots as much as he studied the expanse of music.
